principal_decision_draft.question: Which metric-owned tolerance and non-finite policy determines a meaningful plateau near zero?
principal_decision_draft.premise: The controller uses minimization. A zero historical minimum followed by a positive recent value is regression, while a negative value can be genuine improvement; one global machine epsilon cannot define semantic improvement across differently scaled objectives.

options.name: Metric-owned signed tolerance
options.choice: Normalize objective direction, compute signed gain, then apply configured absolute tolerance near zero and relative tolerance away from zero. A non-finite/unknown score is not scientific convergence; the separate resource ceiling may still stop execution.
options.cost: Medium: metric profiles and serialized rule versions must carry direction and tolerances; avoids scale confusion.

options.name: Single optimizer-wide absolute threshold
options.choice: Keep one configured absolute threshold for all objectives and treat non-finite values under a common explicit stop/unknown rule.
options.cost: Low initial migration; high semantic risk and repeated tuning because income, rates, and normalized losses have different scales.

principal_decision_draft.residual: Neither option normalizes every maximize/minimize objective or establishes that a resource stop is scientific convergence; the selected policy must state both separately.
principal_decision_draft.revisit_falsifier: Reopen if a unit conversion or sign reversal for the same objective changes plateau disposition without changing the underlying improvement, or if a non-finite run is recorded as scientific convergence.
principal_decision_draft.binding_seam: ImprovementPlateau.check plus the objective/metric contract and its persisted rule version.

principal_decision_draft.question: How should a champion remain comparable when suite, split, loop, or data basis changes?
principal_decision_draft.premise: Candidate and evaluation must bind to each other and to an applicable benchmark basis; equal metric names/numbers do not establish comparable evidence.

options.name: Re-evaluate the current champion on each new basis
options.choice: Reject mismatched candidate/evaluation bindings. When suite, split, metric method, or data basis changes, evaluate the current champion on the new basis before comparing candidates.
options.cost: High compute and latency for expensive benchmarks; preserves one continuously comparable champion.

options.name: Maintain a champion per immutable comparison cohort
options.choice: Key champion records by suite/version, split, metric method, and data basis; never compare or promote across cohorts without a new bridge evaluation.
options.cost: Medium storage and API complexity; avoids mandatory reruns but fragments the notion of one global champion.

principal_decision_draft.residual: This establishes technical comparability only; it does not prove evaluator quality or grant any institutional promotion authority.
principal_decision_draft.revisit_falsifier: Reopen if a candidate from another candidate_ref/loop/split or an incompatible suite can alter the pointer, or if an admitted conversion between two suites is shown equivalent but cannot be represented.
principal_decision_draft.binding_seam: ChampionRegistry.consider_promotion, BenchmarkEvaluation binding, SearchLoopRunner caller, and the persisted comparison-cohort identity.

principal_decision_draft.question: Which concurrency envelope must the champion read–compare–publish operation support?
principal_decision_draft.premise: Atomic replacement of one pointer does not serialize the predecessor comparison. A stale writer can overwrite a stronger result; the repository card does not establish production multi-process demand.

options.name: Conditional publish through the store owner
options.choice: Publish only if the predecessor version/digest still matches, then re-read and re-compare on conflict. Keep expensive evaluation outside the transaction.
options.cost: Medium to high: requires a conditional-write primitive from the actual store and explicit conflict handling; supports concurrent writers.

options.name: One serialized publication owner
options.choice: Route all compare-and-publish operations through one existing writer/lock owner; reject or queue other publishers.
options.cost: Medium: simpler storage contract, but adds throughput and availability limits and must prove every writer uses the owner.

principal_decision_draft.residual: Crash durability and multi-host behavior remain unclaimed unless the selected store primitive and deployment mode establish them.
principal_decision_draft.revisit_falsifier: Reopen if a controlled B(score 2)/C(score 3) schedule leaves score 2 current, or if a second process can bypass the chosen serialization owner.
principal_decision_draft.binding_seam: ChampionRegistry predecessor read, comparison, and pointer publication as one owned conditional transition.

principal_decision_draft.question: Does run_id name an immutable completed run or a mutable alias to the latest versioned artifact?
principal_decision_draft.premise: Warm and cold managers must replay the same referenced history. The current cache is keyed only by run_id, while registration can replace the history under that id.

options.name: Immutable run identity
options.choice: Treat a completed run_id as immutable and reject a conflicting re-registration; address the cached history by its immutable ArtifactRef/digest.
options.cost: Low to medium: simple replay semantics, but callers must allocate a new run id for revised history and retain old records.

options.name: Versioned mutable alias
options.choice: Allow a run_id alias to move only by publishing a new versioned ArtifactRef; key cache entries by the referenced digest/version and keep old refs replayable.
options.cost: Medium: supports updates but needs alias history, cache invalidation, and version-aware readers.

principal_decision_draft.residual: Memory eviction policy and the separate TRN-02 live-metadata/distributed-atomicity residuals are not decided here.
principal_decision_draft.revisit_falsifier: Reopen if a warm reader sees stale/new bytes differently from a cold reader for the same immutable ref, or if a legitimate caller must repoint run_id without a versioned ref.
principal_decision_draft.binding_seam: register_run, _eval_cache keying, history loader, and the immutable artifact reference persisted with each run.
principal_decision_draft.scope_note: The source card B133 concerns mutable run_id/cache identity. The Appendix C TRN-02 residual also groups live metadata and distributed atomicity; those are separate residuals, not this decision.

principal_decision_draft.question: May robustness be claimed over the full declared scenario set, or only over a named sampled/early-stopped subset?
principal_decision_draft.premise: Presentation dedupe/top-k truncation must not alter counts of tested scenarios, observed violations, or non-results; adaptive stopping does not automatically estimate the entire space.

options.name: Require complete declared-set accounting
options.choice: Stream occurrence, tested-scenario, missing/non-numeric, and completeness counts before display cap; mark early-stopped or incomplete runs unknown/limited.
options.cost: Medium compute and schema work; may delay a result until the declared set finishes.

options.name: Allow a named sampled estimate
options.choice: Keep bounded/adaptive execution but report the sampling design, inspected denominator, uncertainty, and sampled-score label; never call it full-population robustness.
options.cost: Lower compute and faster feedback; weaker claim and added sampling/uncertainty reporting.

principal_decision_draft.residual: The explored population is not automatically exhaustive; unique issue examples and presentation cap remain separate from occurrence counts.
principal_decision_draft.revisit_falsifier: Reopen if changing collect_top_k changes robustness score for the same completed scenario set, or if an early-stopped sample is presented as complete population coverage.
principal_decision_draft.binding_seam: Robustness aggregator before dedupe/cap, run completeness record, and the surfaced metric name.

principal_decision_draft.question: Is an explicit stored deny a veto, or is promotion_allowed only an advisory baseline overridden by the final evaluator?
principal_decision_draft.premise: A constrained R4 event can persist promotion_allowed=False while the evaluator later returns True from state-only interpretation; ordinary mapper-produced R4 usually emits True. The counterexample does not establish an external release action.

options.name: Treat explicit restriction as a veto
options.choice: Preserve false/restriction as a binding veto; permit only a separately typed, authorized override with reason and scope.
options.cost: Medium: new override evidence/schema and caller migration; conservative when an explicit restriction was intended to bind.

options.name: Make the event flag an advisory baseline
options.choice: Rename it as a baseline/readiness hint and let one evaluator compute final permission; carry any institutional restriction in a separate typed veto field.
options.cost: Medium to high: schema and all readers must migrate; avoids treating an advisory flag as final authority but risks old consumers assuming the old meaning.

principal_decision_draft.residual: Deployment/live-feed applicability in DDM-02 remains unclaimed; this decision resolves field meaning/precedence only, not feed authority or release service behavior.
principal_decision_draft.revisit_falsifier: Reopen if a mapper-produced explicit false is consumed as a veto by a supported caller but the chosen evaluator allows it, or if every supported caller proves the field is advisory and the veto option blocks an authorized path.
principal_decision_draft.binding_seam: ReadinessStateEvent/ModelRegistryReadinessRecord schema, readiness mapper, registry builder/evaluator, and final action consumer.
